findings.title: route-load reset callback (lines 155-237) clears NONE of the five rename vars
findings.detail: Full span: `reset: ({ isSwitch }) => {` opens at 155, closing `},` at 237. Grepping that exact range for "rename" finds exactly one hit — a comment at line 200 (`// \`renameStatus\` are NOT cleared here, per #287 review; only`) — no assignment to any of the five. The callback's unconditional-clear group (outside the `if (isSwitch)` block, lines 160-213) clears reorderError/reorderStatus (160-161), removeError/pendingRemoveId/removePending (167-173), pendingDeactivateId/deactivateRefusal/deactivateActionError/deactivatePending (176-183), inviteActionPending (194), and recordEditorMemberId/recordEditorLookup/recordSaveError/recordStatus (205-213). The `if (isSwitch)` block (221-236) additionally clears showInactive/inactiveRows/inactiveLoadError/inviteLinkByMemberId/inviteErrorByMemberId/withdrawErrorByMemberId. None of the five rename identifiers appear in either group — this is the #297 gap, confirmed at HEAD (`c2829ea`).

findings.title: submitRename, quoted in full (lines 2701-2761) — generation capture is USABLE (no trap here)
Which of the five SHOULD be cleared on switch — reasoned per-var, not by analogy-to-all
findings.detail:
renamePending — SHOULD be cleared unconditionally in `reset` (same treatment as `removePending`/`deactivatePending`, #287, lines 173/183). It feeds `structuralWritePending` (line 2683: `reorderPending || renamePending || removePending`), which disables EVERY structural control (rename/delete/indent/unindent triggers) page-wide via `disabled={structuralWritePending || ...}` at multiple template sites (e.g. 4593). A rename in flight on the OLD collective at switch time currently leaves `renamePending` true forever (its own finally is unconditional per finding above, so on a LATE settle it clears fine, but before that settle the NEW collective's structural controls are wrongly disabled) — this is the live, user-visible half of the #296/#287 defect shape, reproduced for rename.

renamingSectionId — SHOULD be cleared, matching the established "state keyed to data being replaced" principle applied uniformly in this file to per-row armed-ids (`pendingRemoveId` line 168, `pendingDeactivateId` line 176, `recordEditorMemberId` line 205) regardless of whether an id COLLISION across collectives is likely (Entu ids are UUID-shaped and won't collide in practice, so the concrete rendering impact is low — `{#if renamingSectionId === row.id}` at 4467 simply won't match any row in the new tree — but leaving it set is inconsistent with the pattern this file otherwise applies unconditionally, and it costs nothing to clear).

renameValue — SHOULD be cleared alongside renamingSectionId, mirroring the pairing `cancelRename` already enforces (2695-2696 clears both together). Not independently load-bearing (its only render site is gated by `renamingSectionId === row.id`, so it can't leak visibly on its own — `startRename` also overwrites it before display, line 2690), but for consistency with the existing pairing convention it should be cleared with its partner. [speculative: severity — this one is cosmetic/consistency, not a demonstrable user-visible bug on its own.]

renameError — SHOULD be cleared unconditionally, exactly matching `removeError`'s precedent and rationale (lines 162-166: "a failure message naming a section the next tree may not even contain"). `renameError` is the identical shape (`{ id, name }` naming a section) for the identical action-failure concern; the codebase's own comment for removeError is a template for renameError verbatim.

renameStatus — should NOT be cleared on switch. This is a DELIBERATE existing pattern, explicit in the comment at line 200 ("`removeStatus`/`pageCreateStatus`/`renameStatus` are NOT cleared here, per #287 review"), grouping renameStatus with removeStatus and pageCreateStatus as one-off "invisible success" announcements that name a past action's target by value (not by on-screen tree position), contrasted with `reorderStatus`/`recordStatus` which ARE cleared because their text describes on-screen tree/row state that a reload invalidates (see the reorderStatus rationale at lines 156-159: "a previous reorder's alert nor its 'moved to position 2' announcement is about anything on screen any more"). Since `renameStatus`'s text ("section X renamed") doesn't claim anything about currently-rendered state, the file's own established convention is to let it persist across a switch — the actual defect for renameStatus is not the reset-callback omission but the WRITE at line 2732 being ungated (finding above). I did not find independent evidence this deliberate choice is wrong for renameStatus specifically, so I report it as the established, reasoned exception rather than a fifth thing to newly clear. [speculative: whether the #287-review rationale should be revisited is a design call for the fix author/PO, not something I can settle by reading alone.]

findings.title: performReorder — full quote, current line numbers, generation-check inventory
performReparent — full quote, current line numbers, generation-check inventory
Issue #296's claim for reorderPending is CONFIRMED verbatim, both writers; trap check negative for both
findings.detail:
#296's table states: 'reorderPending | Cleared on switch? No | finally guarded? No (both finally clauses) | Flag-clear only — its success and refetch paths are already correctly generation-guarded.' Traced above line-by-line: TRUE for both performReorder and performReparent. Every write branch that touches `sections`, `reorderStatus`, or `reorderError` inside either function is already gated by a `g !== routeLoad.generation` / `g === routeLoad.generation` check (performReorder: 2413, 2425, 2429; performReparent: 2543, 2548, 2583, 2587). The ONLY ungated writes to `reorderPending` itself are the two unconditional `finally` clears (2432, 2590). No other bug shape found in either function beyond the one #296 names.

Trap check (the #287 handleDeactivateConfirm class — a capture sitting after an await that already bumped the counter, making the guard always-true and inert): NOT present in either function. Both `const g = routeLoad.generation;` captures (2396, 2519) sit strictly BEFORE that function's own first `await` (2408, 2536 respectively) — no async call, no `await`, occurs between function entry and the capture line in either case (only synchronous `structuralWritePending`/`currentCfg` checks precede it). Both captures are at a USABLE scope. Fixing the finally blocks is therefore a matter of adding `if (g === routeLoad.generation) reorderPending = false;` in place of the unconditional clear at 2432 and 2590 — reusing the existing `g`, no new capture needed, and no risk of the always-true trap since the capture predates the async work in both functions.

findings.title: reorderPending consumers, direct and via structuralWritePending
findings.detail:
Direct reads/writes of `reorderPending` itself (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte, HEAD):
- 2317: `let reorderPending = $state(false);` — declaration.
- 2397: set true (performReorder entry).
- 2432: clear, unconditional, in performReorder's `finally`.
- 2520: set true (performReparent entry).
- 2590: clear, unconditional, in performReparent's `finally`.
- 2683: `const structuralWritePending = $derived(reorderPending || renamePending || removePending);` — the only place `reorderPending` is read outside its own two writers.
- 4161: `{#if reorderPending}` — a live 'moving...' status region (`data-testid="section-reorder-pending"`, `role="status"`, `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-live="polite"`) rendered directly off the raw flag, not off `structuralWritePending`. This is a SECOND functional consumer beyond the derived value and is itself a UI element that will stay stuck 'busy' post-switch if the flag is left true from an armed-then-abandoned write on the old collective.
All other grep hits naming `reorderPending` (e.g. lines 171, 740, 1734, 1868, 1878, 1918-1925, 1982, 2224, 2334-2336, 2442-2445, 2670, 3051, 3148-3149, 3200, 3823, 4369, 4668-4671) are prose comments referencing the flag by name, not additional functional reads/writes — verified by inspecting each site; the real gating always routes through `structuralWritePending`.

`structuralWritePending` — defined once at 2683 as shown above. Functional (non-comment) consumers, all read-only:
- 2388 — performReorder's own entry guard.
- 2511 — performReparent's own entry guard.
- 1882 — `handleRemoveSection`'s entry guard.
- 2686 — `startRename`'s entry guard.
- 2715 — `submitRename`'s entry guard.
- 2988 — `handlePointerDown`'s entry guard.
- 3158 — `toggleGrab`'s entry guard (inside the null-grab branch).
- Render bindings: 4502 (`draggable={... ? 'false' : 'true'}`), 4506 (class list), 4557 (class list on the drag-handle affordance), 4593 (`disabled={structuralWritePending || renamingSectionId === row.id}`), 4713 and 4732 (`disabled={structuralWritePending || ...}`), 4786 and 4797 (`disabled={structuralWritePending}`), 4816 (`disabled={structuralWritePending || ...}`).
All of these are single-flight backstops that go stale together the moment `reorderPending` is stuck true — a switch that leaves it true post-#294 disables indent/unindent, drag, keyboard-grab, remove, rename-start and rename-submit across the WHOLE new collective's tree, not just the reorder control itself, because they all fold through the one derived boolean.

findings.title: route-load reset() does not clear reorderPending — confirmed absent
findings.detail: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:155-237, the `reset: ({ isSwitch }) => { ... }` callback passed to `createRouteLoadMachine`. Read in full. It unconditionally clears `reorderError` (160) and `reorderStatus` (161) with an explicit comment about the tree being replaced, then goes on to unconditionally clear `removeError`/`pendingRemoveId`/`removePending` (167-173, citing #287), `pendingDeactivateId`/`deactivateRefusal`/`deactivateActionError`/`deactivatePending` (176-183, citing #255/#287), and `inviteActionPending` (194, citing #294's application of 'the other half of #287's two-part discipline'). At NO point in this 83-line callback does `reorderPending` appear — it is the one flag from the original #287 sibling triple that reset() skips entirely, while its own paired transient state (`reorderError`, `reorderStatus`) IS cleared beside it. This directly confirms #296's table cell 'Cleared on switch? No' for `reorderPending`, and shows the omission is a genuine gap relative to precedent already living three lines above it in the same function, not a design choice — every other single-flight pending flag on the page (`removePending`, `deactivatePending`, `inviteActionPending`) gets the identical unconditional clear here.

findings.title: Shared-flag-across-two-writers: no complication for a per-writer conditional-clear guard
findings.detail: [speculative reasoning, built on verified structure] `reorderPending` is written by exactly two functions, `performReorder` (2380-2435) and `performReparent` (2503-2593), and both gate their own ENTRY on `structuralWritePending` (2388, 2511) — which itself reads `reorderPending` (among others) at 2683. Because `structuralWritePending` folds `reorderPending` back into both functions' own entry guards, the two writers are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE by construction: whichever one runs first sets `reorderPending = true` and the other's entry guard then refuses for the whole duration of that write, so they can never be concurrently in-flight on this page (confirmed by the shared page-wide comment at 2442-2445/2667-2683 describing 'one structural write at a time... whichever control started it'). Consequence for the fix: converting each function's own `finally` (2432, 2590) from an unconditional clear to `if (g === routeLoad.generation) reorderPending = false;`, using that SAME function's own entry-captured `g` (2396 / 2519 respectively), introduces no cross-writer hazard — at the moment either finally runs, that function is by construction the only one that has ever set the flag true since its own entry (the other writer was refused at its own entry guard the whole time), so there is no scenario where writer A's finally could be evaluating a generation captured by writer B, or clearing a flag that B is still relying on. The mutual-exclusion property that makes ONE shared flag safe to use for two writers in the first place is the same property that makes a PER-WRITER, per-function generation capture safe to guard that shared flag's clear with — the sharing does not require a THIRD, cross-writer generation value or any additional coordination beyond what each function already does independently. The only actual cross-cutting item is the reset()-side unconditional clear (finding above): that one write is not 'per-writer' at all, it is a single unconditional assignment on collective switch, so it needs no generation check and no writer-specific handling.

findings.title: reinstatePending — declaration, handler, and the same entry-capture trap as pre-#287 handleDeactivateConfirm
deactivateActionError — declaration, both writer catches, and the render-condition asymmetry between the two kinds
findings.detail:
Declaration, `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:921-923`:
```
921: let deactivateActionError = $state<{ memberId: string; kind: 'deactivate' | 'reinstate' } | null>(
922:     null
923: );
```

**Writer catch #1 — `handleDeactivateConfirm`, `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1116-1125`:**
```
1116:     } catch (e) {
1117:         // FAIL-CLOSED (Gama binding): a rejected rights read, or a rejected
1118:         // write, must never leave the deactivate looking like it went through.
1119:         // And fail-LOUD (#255 review F2): the confirm disarms itself and the row
1120:         // is unchanged, so without this alert the tap reads as "nothing happened".
1121:         console.error('roster: deactivate failed', row.memberId, e);
1122:         // #286 — `pendingDeactivateId` is left set here too (the #273 retry
1123:         // convention): the pair sits armed beside `deactivateActionError`
1124:         // above for a direct retry through the same confirm.
1125:         deactivateActionError = { memberId: row.memberId, kind: 'deactivate' };
1126:     } finally {
```
No `if (g === routeLoad.generation …)` (or `isCurrent`) guard wraps line 1125 — confirmed ungated. (This handler DOES have a usable entry capture, `gEntry` at line 1028, already used correctly elsewhere in the same handler — see the sibling reinstatePending finding — so gating this catch, if wanted, only needs to reuse `gEntry`, not add a new capture.)

**Writer catch #2 — `handleReinstate`, `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1237-1242`:**
```
1237:     } catch (e) {
1238:         // #255 review F2 — a failed reinstate produces NO visible change at all
1239:         // otherwise (the row is already in the inactive panel and stays there),
1240:         // so the tap is silently indistinguishable from a dead button.
1241:         console.error('roster: reinstate failed', memberId, e);
1242:         deactivateActionError = { memberId, kind: 'reinstate' };
1243:     } finally {
```
Also confirmed ungated — and this handler has NO usable entry capture at all (see sibling finding), so gating this one requires the same new entry-level capture that the `reinstatePending` finally needs; the two fixes in this handler should share one `gEntry`.

**Is it cleared on switch?** Yes, unconditionally: `reset`'s callback body sets `deactivateActionError = null;` at line 178, outside the `isSwitch` block (so on every load, switch or same-collective refresh alike) — matching the issue table's 'Cleared on switch? Yes' for this flag.

**Render sites — the asymmetry between the two `kind`s:**

- **`kind: 'deactivate'`**, `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3886`:
  ```
  {#if pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId && deactivateActionError?.memberId === row.memberId && deactivateActionError.kind === 'deactivate'}
  ```
  This IS still safe by construction at HEAD: it is co-gated on `pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId`, and `pendingDeactivateId` is cleared unconditionally by `reset` at line 176 (same unconditional-on-every-load treatment as `deactivateActionError` itself). On any switch `pendingDeactivateId` goes to `null`, so this condition can never match any row regardless of what a stale catch later writes into `deactivateActionError`. #287's original finding holds unchanged after #294 — confirmed by re-reading both the render site and the current `reset` body.

- **`kind: 'reinstate'`**, `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:5014` (inside the `{#each inactiveRows as row}` loop starting line 4991):
  ```
  {#if deactivateActionError?.memberId === row.memberId && deactivateActionError.kind === 'reinstate'}
  ```
  This is **NOT** co-gated on anything `reset` clears — no `pendingDeactivateId`-style companion check, and `reinstatePending` (the closest analogue) isn't referenced in this condition at all. It relies solely on `deactivateActionError` itself being cleared, and on `inactiveRows` (isSwitch-gated clear, line 223) no longer containing a matching row. So the 'safe by construction' argument #287 established for the deactivate-kind alert does **not** transfer to the reinstate-kind alert — this is the render-side counterpart of `deactivateActionError`'s two ungated writer catches, and is exactly why gating BOTH catches (not just relying on `reset`) matters for #296, unlike the deactivate-kind case which is arguably already safe by the render gate alone.

findings.title: Runner, command, and current totals (re-pinned)

findings.title: #297 rename quintet: none cleared on switch; a USABLE entry-capture already exists; only the success announcement is ungated (finally is ungated too)
findings.detail: submitRename (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:2700-2758). A usable capture already exists: `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at line 2725, set BEFORE `renamePending = true` (2727) and before the first await (`await renameSection(...)` at 2731) — checked against the #287 trap explicitly: this capture is NOT rebased past any await, so it is safe to reuse as-is; no new capture is required. Per-site guard status: (1) line 2732 `renameStatus = m.roster_section_renamed({ name });` — UNGATED, confirms #297's claim exactly: a rename settling after a switch announces into whichever collective is now on screen. (2) line 2751 `renameError = { id, name };` — already effectively guarded: both branches of the preceding refetch try/catch (lines 2744 and 2749) `return` early `if (g !== routeLoad.generation)`, so renameError is unreachable on a stale generation; no change needed here. (3) the `finally` block (2753-2758): `renamePending = false;` (2753) is UNGATED (unconditional), then `await tick(); document.querySelector(...).focus();` — also unconditional. Per Gama's binding shape rule (issue comments), the flag-clear needs the conditional-write form `if (g === routeLoad.generation) renamePending = false;`; the focus-restoration line's guard is a build-time judgment call (arguably also generation-scoped, since it targets a row that may belong to the stale collective) but is not itself named in the issue's done-when. None of `renamingSectionId`, `renameValue`, `renamePending`, `renameError`, `renameStatus` appear anywhere inside the route-load `reset()` callback (lines 149-235) except in a comment at line 200 noting renameStatus is deliberately NOT cleared there — confirms #297's claim that none of the five are cleared on switch.

findings.title: #296 reorderPending (performReorder/performReparent): entry-capture already usable and success paths already guarded; ONLY the finally clauses are ungated — exactly as filed
findings.detail: performReorder (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:2384-2436): `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at line 2396, captured before `reorderPending = true` (2397) and before the first await (`await reorderSections(...)` at ~2409) — usable, no new capture needed. Success branch already guarded: `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return false;` at line 2412 before writing `reorderStatus`. Refetch-catch branch already guarded at line 2419. Only `reorderPending = false;` in the `finally` at line 2432 is unconditional/ungated. performReparent (lines 2503-2592) is structurally identical: `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at line 2519 (before `reorderPending = true` at 2520 and before the first await at ~2534) is usable; both success-path checks (lines 2537 and 2543, one after `reparentSection` lands and one mid-renumber) are already guarded; the refetch-catch guard at line 2581 is already guarded; only `reorderPending = false;` in the `finally` at line 2590 is unconditional. This exactly matches #296's table entry ("reorderPending: not cleared on switch / finally ungated in both performReorder and performReparent / success and refetch paths already correctly guarded") with no discrepancy found. reorderPending also does not appear anywhere in reset() (lines 149-235) — confirmed not cleared on switch.

findings.title: #296 reinstatePending: NO usable capture exists anywhere in handleReinstate — a genuinely new entry-level capture is required (this is the one flag where the #287 trap's lesson has full bite)
findings.detail: handleReinstate (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1208-1245). The function has zero generation capture before its first await (`await reinstateMember(cfg, memberId)` at line ~1216). The only `const g = routeLoad.generation;` in this function is at line 1226, captured AFTER `await loadForSelected()` has already run and deliberately AFTER that self-bump (mirroring handleDeactivateConfirm's mirror-image reload guard) — it exists solely to guard the subsequent inactive-panel reload (lines 1227-1235), and reusing it for the outer flag-clear would be the exact #287 trap: always-true-post-bump, looks correct, does nothing. A fresh `gEntry`-style capture at function entry (before `reinstatePending = memberId` on line 1212) is required, matching the shape handleDeactivateConfirm's `gEntry` (line 1028) already uses for the same purpose. `reinstatePending = null;` in the finally (line 1244) is fully unconditional today. reinstatePending does not appear in reset() (lines 149-235) — not cleared on switch, confirmed.

findings.title: #296 deactivateActionError: two writer catches, one has a usable capture in scope, the other does not
findings.detail: Two unconditional writes, both confirmed ungated: (1) handleDeactivateConfirm's catch, line 1125: `deactivateActionError = { memberId: row.memberId, kind: 'deactivate' };`. This function already has `const gEntry = routeLoad.generation;` at line 1028, captured at function entry before any await — the SAME capture already reused for `deactivatePending`'s finally-guard at line 1137 (`if (gEntry === routeLoad.generation) deactivatePending = false;`). gEntry is directly reusable here: `if (gEntry === routeLoad.generation) deactivateActionError = {...};`. (2) handleReinstate's catch, line 1242: `deactivateActionError = { memberId, kind: 'reinstate' };`. As established above, handleReinstate has no entry-level capture at all — this write needs the same new entry-scope capture that reinstatePending's finally-guard will also need (one new `gEntry` serves both). Note deactivateActionError IS cleared unconditionally in reset() (line 178, outside the `if (isSwitch)` block) — matches #296's table ("Cleared on switch? Yes"); the bug is purely the two writer catches, not the reset callback.

findings.title: page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts (#287) in full — the reusable house pattern for #296/#297
findings.detail: Read in full (539 lines). Reusable machinery, with exact line numbers: `deferred<T>()` (228-236) returns {promise, resolve, reject} for a release-controlled mock. `q(container, testid)` (238-240) is the data-testid query helper. `flush = () => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))` (246) drains one microtask tick after a gate resolves. `setAuthedWithTwoCollectives()` (173-190) seeds two fixture collectives ('polyphony' as ORG_A / 'other-choir' as ORG_B) via authStore/collectiveState/urlCollectiveDbStore/selectedCollectiveDbStore, mirrored near-verbatim in page.roster-arrange-stale-success.spec.ts and the deactivate spec's own copy. Fixtures: treeA()/treeB() (141-154) disjoint SectionNode[] per collective; rowsA()/rowsB() (160-171) disjoint RosterRow[], every member UNASSIGNED so rows sit under the Unassigned toggle and deactivate triggers always render. beforeEach (192-212) wires loadRosterMock/listSectionsMock to branch on cfg.db, and resolves every other write mock immediately by default — a test that wants to HOLD a specific write overrides that one mock's `mockImplementation` to return an unsettled promise via `deferred()`. Render/switch drivers, arrange-mode: `renderInArrangeMode()` (248-260) renders, waits for roster-groups, clicks roster-view-chip-arrange, waits for roster-arrange-list. `switchToOtherChoirArrange(container)` (262-269) sets `selectedCollectiveDbStore.set('other-choir')`, waits for arrange-row-sec-b1, then asserts arrange-row-sec-alto is gone (B fully on screen before anything stale settles). `startHeldRemoveOnA(container)` (272-281) clicks section-remove-sec-tenor, waits for the confirm control, clicks confirm, waits for `deleteMock` call count — arms + confirms the write into the held gate. Render/switch drivers, groups-mode: `renderGroupsRoster()` (285-297), `switchToOtherChoirGroups(container)` (299-311, which re-clicks section-toggle-unassigned after the switch since it collapses groups), `startHeldDeactivate(container, memberId, nthWrite)` (315-324, parameterized by expected call count so it composes across A-then-B arms). The three-consequence structure a new spec should mirror per flag: STALE DISABLE (assert a B control's `disabled`/`draggable` immediately after switch, write still held), CROSS-COLLECTIVE ANNOUNCEMENT (assert the live-region text is empty after the stale write resolves post-switch — this is the one #297 most needs, for renameStatus), LATE-SETTLE CLOBBER (arm a second, genuine write on B via mockImplementationOnce sequencing of two gates, resolve A's stale gate, assert B's armed pair/flag survives and no double-fire, then resolve B's gate and assert it completes honestly). A new spec for renamePending/reorderPending/reinstatePending/deactivateActionError would import this file's pattern wholesale but needs its own held-write driver per control (arrange-mode rename trigger + confirm-on-Enter for rename; the existing performReorder/performReparent keyboard-drop or indent-click sequences already in page.roster-arrange-stale-success.spec.ts for reorder/reparent; startHeldDeactivate's structure adapted to member-reinstate-{id} for reinstate).

findings.title: Full list of existing specs touching rename/reorder/reparent/reinstate/deactivateActionError, split by genuine exercise vs. mock-boilerplate-only
findings.detail: RENAME — genuinely exercised: page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts (renameMock assertions at lines 245,247,277,283,311,541), page.roster-arrange-whole-field.spec.ts (lines 279,295,332,345,440,479 — asserts renameMock NOT called as a side-effect check, not a rename-flow test per se). page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts mocks renameSection in its module mocks but never exercises rename in a test (grep shows no fireEvent against a rename control). findings.title: An existing spec ALREADY switches collectives mid-write for reorderPending/reparent — but it exercises the already-fixed (#264) success-announcement guard, not the #296 finally-clear bug; no narrowing of #296's scope
findings.detail: page.roster-arrange-stale-success.spec.ts (lines 187-285) is the one file that constructs a genuine held-write-across-a-switch race for reorder AND reparent: `switchToOtherChoir()` (201-208) plus a release-controlled reorderMock (213-251, 'performReorder' test) and reparentMock (253-284, 'performReparent' test). Both tests hold the write, switch to 'other-choir' while it is in flight, then resolve the write and assert: (1) the live-region status text stays EMPTY (statusText, line 248/276) — this exercises the try-block generation check at lines 2412/2537 (already present per #264 item 4, already passing), NOT the finally at 2432/2590; (2) for reparent, the follow-up renumber (reorderMock) is not called (line 282) — again the try-block guard, not the finally. Neither test asserts anything about reorderPending's value, about a B-side control's disabled/draggable state, or about a second genuine write started on B before A's stale settle (no LATE-SETTLE CLOBBER construction for reorder/reparent exists anywhere). So: #296's reorderPending scope is NOT narrower than filed — the specific defect (unconditional finally-clear either falsely re-enabling B's controls after a load-time stale-disable, or clobbering a genuine second write's flag) remains completely unexercised by any existing spec. Separately, since reorderPending is never cleared in reset() either, this stale-success spec's own `switchToOtherChoir` — which waits for B's arrange rows to render before proceeding — would today be racing against structuralWritePending still reading true from A's held write; the spec happens to not assert on any control's disabled state during that window, so it passes regardless, but it means the STALE-DISABLE half of the bug is silently live and unpinned even in the one file that already does a mid-write switch for this flag.

findings.title: REINSTATE: an existing spec switches collectives while reinstatePending is genuinely still true (not just "mock resolves instantly") — but asserts only on inactiveRows, not on reinstatePending/disabled state; #296's scope not narrowed
findings.detail: page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts, 'a POST-REINSTATE panel reload that settles after a switch writes NOTHING' (lines 1212-1243). handleReinstate's own `finally { reinstatePending = null; }` sits AFTER the entire try block, which includes `await loadForSelected()` and then the inactive-panel reload (`await loadInactiveRoster(cfg)`, held via `holdInactiveLoads()` in this test). Because the panel reload is held open at the point `switchToOtherChoir(container)` runs (line 1230), reinstatePending is provably still true across the switch in this test — genuinely mid-write, not a same-tick artifact. However the test's assertions (lines 1234-1242) check only that A's stale rows do not leak into B's reopened inactive panel (`inactive-member-row-m9` absent, panel shows B's own empty truth) — nothing in the test reads `member-reinstate-*` disabled state or otherwise pins reinstatePending's value. So this test would keep passing unchanged whether or not reinstatePending's finally is generation-guarded; it does not cover, and therefore does not narrow, the STALE-DISABLE / LATE-SETTLE-CLOBBER behavior #296 files for reinstatePending. RENAME has no equivalent at all: no spec in the repo calls `selectedCollectiveDbStore.set(...)` anywhere in a test that also touches renameMock/renamingSectionId — confirmed via combined grep across every rename-touching file. DEACTIVATE-ACTION-ERROR: no spec switches collectives while either writer catch's error path is in flight — the two-collective describe blocks in page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts (lines 1080-1270) construct races around loadInactiveRoster settles and reinstateMember/deactivateMember successes only, never a rejection.

findings.title: COMPLETENESS ANSWER: #297 + #296 do NOT close the class — at least a 5th issue is needed
findings.detail: Full flag inventory below. #287 fixed removePending/deactivatePending; #294 correctly applied the same discipline to inviteActionPending (both halves: reset-clear + generation-guarded settle — verified clean). #297 (renamePending/renamingSectionId/renameValue/renameError/renameStatus) and #296 (reorderPending, reinstatePending, deactivateActionError's two catches) each target real, confirmed gaps. But five more instances of the exact same defect shape survive untouched by either issue's stated scope: (1) deactivateRefusal's write in handleDeactivateConfirm's REFUSAL branch (not a catch — a mid-try write, distinct from #296's two named catches) is ungated; (2) removeError's catch-write in handleRemoveSection is ungated; (3) reorderError's catch-writes in both performReorder and performReparent are ungated (separate from reorderPending's finally, which #296 does cover); (4) sectionWriteError + its writer handleCreate has ZERO generation-guard machinery of any kind and is never cleared in reset(); (5) pageCreateError/pageCreateStatus + their writer submitPageCreate also has ZERO generation-guard machinery and are never cleared in reset(). Items 4 and 5 are the most severe — worse than anything #287 originally fixed, since there is no partial/wrong guard to trap into, just total absence. A fifth issue is warranted, at minimum covering items 4-5; items 1-3 are smaller companions that could ride along.

findings.title: sectionWriteError / handleCreate: no generation guard at all (new finding, unnamed by #296/#297)
findings.detail: sectionWriteError declared line 128, never cleared in reset() (absent from the whole 155-236 block). Its sole writer, handleCreate (lines 2012-2078), captures no generation at all — no `const g = routeLoad.generation`, no isCurrent() check anywhere in the function. Both awaits (createSection line 2037, assignMemberSection line 2069) can outlive a collective switch; a stale settle writes `sections = insertSectionNode(...)` (line 2062) and/or `sectionWriteError = {...}` (2022/2040/2074) straight onto whatever collective is now on screen. Render gate (`sectionWriteError?.memberId === row.memberId`, line 3798) happens to mask the error banner cross-collective only because memberIds don't collide across different dbs — but the tree-mutation write (line 2062) is not row-scoped and is a real state leak.

findings.title: pageCreateError / pageCreateStatus / submitPageCreate: no generation guard at all (new finding, unnamed by #296/#297)
findings.detail: pageCreateError (line 2098) and pageCreateStatus (line 2107) are never cleared in reset(), and their writer submitPageCreate (lines 2154-2214) — like handleCreate — has no generation capture or isCurrent() check anywhere. `sections = insertSectionNode(...)` at line 2210 is unconditional; a stale create settling after a switch inserts a section into the tree of whatever collective is now selected. pageCreateOpen/pageCreateName/pageCreateParentId are also left un-reset, though those are lower-severity (form-open cosmetic state).

findings.title: deactivateRefusal ungated write in the REFUSAL branch — a third gap in handleDeactivateConfirm beyond #296's two named catches
findings.detail: deactivateRefusal (decl line 910) is correctly cleared in reset() (line 177), but its write at line 1064 — inside the try block's refusal branch (`if (blockers.length > 0) { deactivateRefusal = {...}; return; }`) — sits after two awaits (resolveMyLibraryId line 1057, listDeactivateBlockers line 1058) with no gEntry check before it, even though gEntry IS captured at a usable, before-first-await scope in this same function (line 1028) and IS correctly used for the success path (line 1080) and the finally (line 1137). #296's issue text names only the catch at line 1125 (deactivateActionError) — this refusal-branch write is a distinct, unnamed third gap in the same function, and the fix is trivial (reuse the already-usable gEntry, same as the adjacent success-path checkpoint).

findings.title: removeError ungated catch-write in handleRemoveSection (new finding, unnamed)
findings.detail: removeError (decl 885) is correctly cleared in reset() (line 167), and removePending's finally (line 2007) is correctly generation-guarded via g captured at line 1921 (usable, before the line-1935 await) — this is #287's fixed pair. But the catch's terminal write `removeError = { name, kind: ... }` at line 1997 is unconditional/ungated, even though the SAME catch block's refetch immediately above it (lines 1985-1993) IS guarded with the same g. removeError is a page-level (not row-scoped) banner (`{#if removeError}` at line 4149), so a stale settle can show a wrong-collective removal-failure banner after a switch.

findings.title: reorderError ungated catch-writes in performReorder and performReparent (new finding, unnamed — distinct from reorderPending's finally which #296 does cover)
findings.detail: reorderError (decl 2326) is cleared in reset() (line 160). #296 correctly identifies reorderPending's finally (performReorder line 2432, performReparent line 2590) as ungated while the success paths (2413; 2543/2548) are already guarded via g captured usably at 2396/2519. But the catch blocks' `reorderError = true` writes (line 2422 in performReorder, line 2579 in performReparent) are ALSO unconditional/ungated — same g is available and used for the refetch immediately below each, just not for this first write. reorderError is page-level (`{#if reorderError}`, line 4134), so this is a real cross-collective banner leak, structurally identical to removeError's gap above.

findings.title: #297 scope confirmed exactly as briefed: renamePending group entirely un-reset, renameStatus success write ungated
findings.detail: renamingSectionId (2655), renameValue (2656), renamePending (2657), renameError (2660), renameStatus (2665) — NONE appear anywhere in reset() (absent from 155-236). submitRename (2701-2761): g is captured at line 2725, usably (before the first await at line 2731) — a good, reusable capture, NOT the #287 trap shape (unlike the deactivate gEntry precedent, this one is genuinely usable as-is). renameStatus's success write (line 2732) is unconditional — confirmed ungated exactly as #297 states. Additionally (not explicitly named by #297's text but same function, same g): renameError's write at line 2751 is also unconditional/ungated, and renamePending's finally (line 2753) is unconditional — both need `if (g === routeLoad.generation) ...`. The focus-restoration lines after it (2757-2759) should stay unconditional per the finally-shape precedent (Gama's ruling) — only the flag/error writes need gating, not the whole finally block.

findings.title: #296 scope confirmed exactly as briefed: reorderPending's finallys, reinstatePending's total absence, deactivateActionError's two catches
findings.detail: reorderPending (decl 2317): absent from reset(); both finallys (2432, 2590) unconditional while success paths are already guarded — matches #296 verbatim. reinstatePending (decl 1206): absent from reset() entirely; handleReinstate (1208-1246) has NO generation capture anywhere in the function — not even a stale/wrong-scope one, so this is the 'no usable capture exists' case: a brand-new entry-level `const g = routeLoad.generation` must be added (there is nothing to trap into, unlike deactivatePending's gEntry precedent). Its finally (`reinstatePending = null;`, line 1244) and its catch-write (`deactivateActionError = {...}`, line 1242) are both currently unconditional. deactivateActionError (decl 921): correctly cleared in reset() (line 178); its two writer catches are handleDeactivateConfirm's (line 1125, where gEntry IS available and usable — line 1028, precedent already proven correct via the finally at 1137) and handleReinstate's (line 1242, where no capture exists at all — needs the new one). Exactly '#296 = ... deactivateActionError (two ungated writer catches)' as briefed.

findings.title: recordSavingMemberId's deliberate exclusion still holds, confirmed at HEAD
findings.detail: recordSavingMemberId (decl 1395) is confirmed still NOT cleared in reset() — the comment at lines 208-212 states this is deliberate ('the save's own finally clears it, and only when it still names that save's row, so it self-heals on settle'). Verified in handleSaveMemberRecord: finally at line 1722 reads `if (recordSavingMemberId === memberId) recordSavingMemberId = null;` — an identity check, not a generation check, which is correct here since the row/memberId identity itself is the right disambiguator (unlike a boolean flag, this one already names which write it belongs to). recordSaveError (1416) and recordEditorMemberId/recordEditorLookup are correctly cleared in reset() (207/205-206) and their catch (line 1697) is properly guarded before either write (1708/1716) via `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g) || recordEditorMemberId !== memberId) return;`. No bug in this handler.

findings.title: inviteActionPending / inviteErrorByMemberId / withdrawErrorByMemberId / inviteLinkByMemberId: #294's handling confirmed fully correct, no residual bug
findings.detail: inviteActionPending (107) is cleared unconditionally in reset() (line 194, correctly NOT gated on isSwitch since it also must clear on a same-collective reload). handleMintInvite/handleWithdrawInvite (1274-1338) each capture g at a usable point (1279/1314, before their first await) and use the early-return shape correctly in both try and catch (1282/1288/1317/1324, all before any write) and the conditional-write shape correctly in finally (1299/1336). inviteErrorByMemberId/withdrawErrorByMemberId/inviteLinkByMemberId are all isSwitch-gated in reset() (233-235) — correct, since these mint/error states are per-collective identity-scoped per the doc comment at lines 92-99. No fix needed here; cited only as a working precedent to compare the broken cases against.

findings.title: inactiveLoadError / toggleInactive: confirmed correct, no bug
findings.detail: inactiveLoadError (1162) is cleared under isSwitch in reset() (line 224). toggleInactive (1164-1192) captures g at line 1180, before its only await (1183), and both the success path (1184-1185) and catch (1187-1190) are guarded with `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g)) return;` before any write. No fix needed.

findings.title: Non-issue: grabRefocusPending / grabbedSectionId / draggedSectionId are synchronous UI state, not in scope of this defect class
findings.detail: grabRefocusPending (3074) is a plain (non-$state) synchronous focus-bookkeeping flag with no server round-trip spanning it, cleared synchronously within the same keyboard-handler tick. grabbedSectionId (3065) and draggedSectionId (2791) are synchronous drag/keyboard-grab UI state keyed to section ids from the currently-rendered tree; the actual network writes they trigger route through performReorder/performReparent, which carry their own (separately-assessed) guards. None of the three match the task's grep patterns (Pending/pending/inFlight/Busy/Saving/Error) and none hold a flag across an async collective-switch gap, so they are excluded from the defect class this sweep targets.

findings.title: Preflight: repo/HEAD confirmed, no drift since #294
findings.detail: origin is https://github.com/mvox-dev/mvox-app.git (mvox-app.git — proceeded). HEAD is caa5a53 (`chore(#280,#244): pipeline args`), two commits after #294's merge c2829ea. `git diff --stat c2829ea HEAD -- src/routes/roster/+page.svelte messages/` is EMPTY — the two commits since #294 touch an unrelated issue (#280/#244); the file content and line numbers below are current at true HEAD. `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte` is 5034 lines.

findings.title: #297 renamePending group: none of the five vars cleared on switch; entry-capture in submitRename is already USABLE (no #287-style trap)
findings.detail: State decls: `renamingSectionId` :2655, `renameValue` :2656, `renamePending` :2657, `renameError` :2660, `renameStatus` :2665. The route-load `reset` callback (:155-236) does NOT touch any of the five — confirmed by absence in that range and by its own comment at :200 ('`removeStatus`/`pageCreateStatus`/`renameStatus` are NOT cleared here, per #287 review'). `submitRename` (:2701-2761) captures `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at :2725 — BEFORE `renamePending = true` (:2727) and before the function's first await, `await renameSection(...)` (:2731). This capture is at a USABLE scope (unlike #287's original `handleDeactivateConfirm` trap) and is already correctly used to guard the catch's refetch/`sections` writes at :2744 and :2748. No new capture is required for this handler; the fix is to (a) clear the five vars in `reset`, and (b) extend the SAME `g` to guard the two writes below that currently skip it.

findings.title: #297: renameStatus success write AND renameError catch write are both ungated by `g`
findings.detail: Confirmed ungated at settle: `renameStatus = m.roster_section_renamed({ name })` at :2732 (the success announcement #297 explicitly flags) has no `g` check before it — unlike `performReorder`'s success branch (:2413), which #294 already guards. Also ungated, and NOT called out verbatim in #297's acceptance text: `renameError = { id, name }` at :2751 — this line sits AFTER the inner refetch try/catch's own `g` checks (:2744, :2748) but is itself unconditional, so a rename that failed on a since-left collective can still paint `arrange-rename-error-{row.id}` (role=alert, :4828) — self-limiting only because `renameError.id` won't match any row id in the new tree. `renamePending = false` in the outer `finally` (:2753) is also unconditional — same shape as #296's `reorderPending`/`reinstatePending` gap.

findings.title: #296 reorderPending: entry capture already USABLE and already reused for the success paths; only the two `finally` clears need it
findings.detail: `performReorder` (:2380-2435) captures `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at :2396, before `reorderPending = true` (:2397) and before the first await `await reorderSections(...)` (:2408) — USABLE scope. Already reused to guard the success write (`if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return false;` at :2413) and the refetch-reconcile writes in the catch (:2425, :2429). `performReparent` (:2503-2593) is identical in shape: `g` captured at :2519 before `reorderPending = true` (:2520) and before its first await (:2536); already guards its success/renumber writes at :2543/:2548 and its catch's refetch at :2583/:2587. In BOTH functions the only ungated write is `reorderPending = false;` in the `finally` (:2432 and :2590) — matches #296's table exactly ('success paths are already correctly generation-guarded', only the `finally` clauses are not). No new capture needed; reuse the existing `g` as a conditional write per the #260/#287 finally-shape precedent (Gama's binding ruling on issues #296/#297: `if (g === routeLoad.generation) reorderPending = false;`, NOT an early return inside the finally).

findings.title: #296 — related-but-out-of-issue-scope gap: reorderError/reparentPartial writes in the catch are also unconditional
findings.detail: In both `performReorder`'s catch (:2421-2422, `reorderError = true;`) and `performReparent`'s catch (:2579-2580, `reorderError = true; reparentPartial = moveLanded;`), these two writes happen BEFORE any `g` check — only the subsequent `sections = fresh`/`sections = before` writes are guarded (:2425/:2429, :2583/:2587). `section-reorder-error` (role=alert, :4145) is rendered unconditionally in the general ready-state body (not admin-gated, not per-row), so a stale-collective reorder/reparent failure can paint this alert into whatever collective is now on screen. Not named in #296's three-row table (which lists reorderPending only) — flagging as directly relevant to the A11Y axis's 'stale write / stale region' question, for the dev team's judgment on whether it's in scope for this pass.

findings.title: #296 reinstatePending: NO usable entry capture exists — a NEW capture is required (this IS the #287-trap case)
findings.detail: `handleReinstate` (:1208-1246) has no generation capture at function entry. Its only capture, `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at :1226, sits AFTER `await reinstateMember(...)` (:1215) and AFTER `await loadForSelected()` (:1218) — both of which can bump the generation counter — so `g` is scoped (correctly) ONLY to the trailing inactive-panel reload (:1227-1236), exactly mirroring `handleDeactivateConfirm`'s narrower `g` (:1105) vs its entry-level `gEntry` (:1028). Reusing this `g` for the catch (`deactivateActionError = { memberId, kind: 'reinstate' }`, :1242) or the `finally` (`reinstatePending = null;`, :1244) would reproduce the exact #287 trap: a guard that reads as correct but is always-true-post-bump and does nothing. A NEW entry-level capture (e.g. `gEntry` immediately after the `:1209` early-return, mirroring `handleDeactivateConfirm`'s `gEntry`) is required to guard both sites. `reinstatePending` is also NOT cleared anywhere in `reset` (:155-236) — confirmed by absence.

findings.title: #296 deactivateActionError's two writer catches: one has a usable entry capture sitting unused, the other has none
findings.detail: Site 1 — `handleDeactivateConfirm`'s catch, `deactivateActionError = { memberId: row.memberId, kind: 'deactivate' };` at :1125: `gEntry` IS captured at function entry (:1028), before the first await (:1057), and is ALREADY used to guard the `finally`'s `deactivatePending = false` (:1137, `if (gEntry === routeLoad.generation)`) — that guard is #287's, already shipped. The fix here is only to extend the SAME `gEntry` to the catch write at :1125; no new capture, no trap. Site 2 — `handleReinstate`'s catch, `deactivateActionError = { memberId, kind: 'reinstate' };` at :1242: no usable capture exists (see previous finding) — needs the new entry-level `gEntry`. `deactivateActionError` itself IS cleared unconditionally in `reset` at :178 (matches #296's table: 'Cleared on switch: Yes').

findings.title: LOCALES — every key these paths write into a live region/alert exists in all four bundles; no new key needed
findings.detail: Verified present with matching interpolation params in messages/en.json, et.json, lv.json, uk.json (grep confirmed all four for each): `roster_section_renamed` (en :217/et :216/lv :216/uk :216), `roster_section_rename_failed` (:218/217/217/217), `roster_section_moved` (:195/194/194/194), `roster_section_indented` (:212/211/211/211), `roster_section_unindented` and `roster_section_unindented_top` (:213-214/212-213/…), `roster_section_reorder_failed` (:192/191/191/191), `roster_section_reparent_partial` (:193/192/192/192), `roster_section_reorder_pending` (:200/199/199/199), `roster_member_deactivate_failed` (:230/229/229/229), `roster_member_reinstate_failed` (:231/230/230/230). Both fixes are pure-suppression (guard an existing write, do not change any copy) — as expected, NO new locale key is needed for #296 or #297.

findings.title: A11Y — live-region/alert map for every flag in scope, with politeness and stale-text-clearing risk
findings.detail: PAGE-LEVEL, unconditional (mounted from first render, NOT gated by `admin`, NOT per-row — the sharp half of the bug class): `roster-reorder-status` (role=status aria-live=polite sr-only, :3995) holds `reorderStatus`; `roster-section-rename-status` (role=status aria-live=polite sr-only, :4052) holds `renameStatus`. Because both feeding writes are settle-time and (per findings above) NOT generation-guarded on their success paths, a stale collective's confirmed rename/reorder can announce into whatever collective is CURRENTLY on screen regardless of that viewer's rights there — exactly #297's stated defect. `section-reorder-error` (role=alert, :4145, general ready-state body, not admin-gated) holds `reorderError`-driven text — same page-level exposure (see finding above). PER-ROW, self-limiting by id match (a stale write's memberId/section-id from the old collective essentially never matches a row in the new one, since Entu ids are per-database): `arrange-rename-error-{row.id}` (role=alert, :4828, inside admin-gated arrange block :4251); `member-deactivate-failed-{row.memberId}` (role=alert, :3894/3896, inside admin-gated block :3813, additionally gated on `pendingDeactivateId===row.memberId`); `member-reinstate-failed-{row.memberId}` (role=alert, :5018/5020, inside admin-gated inactive-panel block :4964). `section-reorder-pending` (role=status aria-busy=true aria-live=polite, :4169) is a live indicator on the boolean flag itself, not text content — clearing the flag correctly (this fix) removes the indicator; no leftover text to clear. CONCLUSION on 'does suppressing leave stale text': for the two unconditional page-level status divs, YES — guarding the WRITE (not announcing) is necessary but a belated correct-and-empty reset is not automatic, since `renameStatus`/`reorderStatus` are strings that persist until the NEXT successful write on the new collective sets them; the existing `reset()` callback already unconditionally blanks `reorderStatus`/`reorderError`/`reparentPartial` (:160-161) and does NOT blank `renameStatus`/`renameError` (per #287 review, :200) — so on a switch, any stale `renameStatus`/`renameError` text from the OLD collective is left standing until overwritten, a second, load-time half of #297's gap worth confirming is intended to be added to `reset()`.

findings.title: RIGHTS — rename/reorder/reparent/reinstate/deactivate are admin-gated, NOT owner-gated after #294; admin is resolved per-collective
findings.detail: The arrange-mode block housing rename (:4591)/indent/unindent (:4710/4729) is gated `{#if admin === 'admin'}` at :4251 (matches the file's own comment on the Arrange chip being 'conditionally rendered for non-admins', :564). The deactivate trigger is gated `{#if admin === 'admin' && row.personId !== selected?.personId}` at :3813. The inactive/reinstate panel is gated `{#if admin === 'admin' && status === 'ready'}` at :4964. #294's `_owner`-tier gating (`ownerTier === 'owner'`, :3688; the invite-owner-only note at :4112) is SCOPED ONLY to the invite mint/re-send/withdraw controls — confirmed both by the file's own doc comment (:85-90: 'the three CONTROLS (kutsu/saada uuesti/tühista kutse) gate on `_owner` alone') and by grep: `ownerTier` never appears near the rename/reorder/deactivate/reinstate sites. `resolveAdmin`/`AdminState` (src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:1-60) resolves admin off the DATABASE ENTITY's `_owner`/`_editor` lists, matched by personId — i.e. PER COLLECTIVE (per #161's 'collective = database' ruling), not a global role. NARROWING EFFECT: this does not narrow the bug to owners — any admin of two-or-more collectives can hit it, a strictly larger population than owner-only, and admin status can genuinely differ between the two collectives being switched between (admin in A, not-admin in B) since it's re-resolved per database entity on every `load` (:264-301).

findings.title: MULTI-COLLECTIVE — switch mechanism confirmed unchanged at HEAD after #294: one route, one reset callback, one generation counter, no remount
findings.detail: Confirmed by direct read of :149-366 and by the empty diff vs c2829ea noted above: `createRouteLoadMachine` (:149-351) still owns a single `reset({isSwitch})` callback (:155-236), a single generation counter (`routeLoad.generation`) and `isCurrent()`/`isCurrent(g)` co-guard, invoked from one `$effect` keyed on `selected` (:357-366) that calls `loadForSelected()` — the component is never remounted on a collective switch (soft nav), so every `$state` declared in the script block survives across switches exactly as #287/#296/#297 describe. #294 extended the SAME machinery rather than building a parallel one for its own `inviteActionPending` (unconditional clear in `reset`, :194, plus its own generation-guarded settle elsewhere) — that is itself the in-file precedent Gama's #296/#297 comments point to for the two-part discipline (entry capture + conditional finally-write) this fix must reuse.

findings.title: Guard-spelling/shape ruling from the issue threads (binding on both #296 and #297)
findings.detail: Per the PO/dev comment exchange on both issues (read via `gh issue view 296/297 --comments`): at HEAD c2829ea the file carries `routeLoad.isCurrent(g)` 18×, `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` 10×, and the conditional-write form `if (g === routeLoad.generation) <write>;` 3×. The binding rule (Gama, superseding two earlier self-corrections): SPELLING (isCurrent(g) vs the inline comparison) is cosmetic — match immediate neighbours, no new fourth spelling. SHAPE is semantic and dictated by position — early return in try/catch, conditional write in finally (an early return inside a finally would skip the rest of that block, e.g. `handleRemoveSection`'s focus restoration, and could discard a pending return/throw) — existing mixed sites must NOT be normalised to one form.
